why_it_is_left_refused.not_a_numeric_gap: no contract is unimplemented and no stub was written: the 39-name refusal is gone and the remaining refusal is capacity, quoted
why_it_is_left_refused.the_plan_names_the_fix: section 3.3: TA-DS41-HBM is the cluster profile 'with the node count raised until 307.5 GB of weights plus the session KV fit, and the Engram tables in HOST MEMORY as DeepSeek serves them'.  The 307.5 GB already excludes the Engram set, so the plan's own comparator presumes a host-resident weight store
why_it_is_left_refused.what_is_missing: compiler/backends/hbm_sram has no host-resident WEIGHT store.  'host' residence exists there only for host input/output windows (plan.py line 673 and _place_activations); a weight group is replicated or node_sharded and nothing else, and every weight object is emitted with StorageClass.HBM (lower.py line 841)
why_it_is_left_refused.why_not_added_here: the backend is model-blind by design: residency is derived from whether an operand's tensor view carries the 'node' selector (plan.py _assign_weight_residency), and nothing in it may know which tensor is an Engram table.  The only model-blind rules available are (a) a greedy 'move the largest replicated groups to host until the node fits', which silently puts arbitrary weights behind a 1-2 us PCIe/RDMA round trip the backend cannot know is hideable -- section 3.4 prices exactly that hop and says the layer-1 Engram module can hide it behind only about 1.8 us of work -- and (b) a capability field naming a role, which is model knowledge in the capability.  The ROM array can decide it because deepseek_v41_array.py is a MODEL-AWARE backend and reads V41_FLASH_PROFILE; engram_residency prices all three placements there and host wins.  Choosing (a) here would let any oversized model 'fit' by pushing weights off-node, which is a placement claim the deployment cannot support
